findings.claim: In SpanFlusher.join(), when the deadline expires the `break` exits the per-process loop before terminate() runs for the current and remaining flusher processes, leaving them running after join returns during shutdown/rebalance.

verifier.reason: In SpanFlusher.join() at src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:337-347, when deadline has expired the check `if remaining_time <= 0: break` (lines 340-341) exits the loop before `process.terminate()` (lines 346-347) is reached. Consequently, once `next_step.join(timeout)` or waiting on an earlier process exhausts the deadline, the current and all remaining flusher processes are not terminated and can remain running after join() returns during shutdown or rebalance.

findings.claim: The isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) guard before process.kill() in the restart path (_ensure_processes_alive) is always False for spawn-context SpawnProcess objects, so hung or unhealthy processes are never killed before replacements start. The pre-PR code called kill() unconditionally.

verifier.reason: In src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:53,105, SpanFlusher spawns workers via multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process, which produces multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess instances (a sibling of multiprocessing.context.Process under BaseProcess, not a subclass). Consequently, the isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) guard in _ensure_processes_alive at src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:254-255 always evaluates to False, so hung or unhealthy processes are never killed before _create_process_for_shards starts replacements at line 259.

findings.claim: In join(), terminate() sits behind the same isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) check, which is always False for SpawnProcess, so flusher processes are never terminated on shutdown or rebalance.

verifier.reason: In src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:53,105, flusher processes are created via multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process (SpawnProcess), which inherits from multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess rather than multiprocessing.Process. Consequently, the isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) check guarding process.terminate() in join() at src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:346-347 (the same check used at lines 254-255) is always False, so flusher processes are never terminated on shutdown or rebalance.

findings.claim: _create_process_for_shard (lines 127-132) has no callers in src/ or tests/ and only delegates to _create_process_for_shards, so it is dead code.

verifier.reason: In src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:127-132, SpanFlusher._create_process_for_shard only looks up the shard in self.process_to_shards_map and delegates to self._create_process_for_shards. Both process creation sites in SpanFlusher (_create_processes at line 84 and _ensure_processes_alive at line 259) call _create_process_for_shards directly, and neither factory.py nor the SpanFlusher tests call _create_process_for_shard, leaving it dead code introduced by the multi-shard-per-process refactor.

findings.claim: The docstring 'Creates one process per shard' does not match the default deployment, where the CLI default of 1 runs all shards in one process. The comments at lines 178 and 235 also do not match the code.

verifier.reason: The SpanFlusher docstring at src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:32 claims it 'Creates one process per shard', but the CLI option '--flusher-processes' defaults to 1 (src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py:432-437), so flusher.py:51,60-66 assigns all shards to a single process by default. Additionally, flusher.py:178 describes updating healthy_since for all shards when line 179 updates a single per-process Value, and flusher.py:235 says 'Check if any shard handled by this process is unhealthy' directly above 'cause = "hang"' after the elif at lines 231-234 already checked the single per-process timestamp.
